about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Mar rallied into the close to ~82.9, clearing Tuesday's highs and the 82.7 resistance as a weaker dollar and firmer crude helped outside money back in. No new supply or demand data; old-crop Mar/May keeps leaning on Texas Plains losses, but high-grade certs stay a two-sided risk for longs.
events: Dollar index slips, firmer crude (WSJ, Pro Farmer)

sugar.fundamental: Mar held its gains near ~18.4, above the 100-day average, with the firmer real still discouraging Brazilian mill export hedging. No fresh centre-south crush or mix figures, so the move remains currency and short covering rather than a change in the Brazil supply picture.
events: Real firm vs the dollar; dollar index weaker (Yahoo Finance, WSJ)

coffee.fundamental: Mar recovered to ~268.6 (+2.6%) from the morning dip, helped by the firmer real and a weaker dollar. Nothing has changed on deliverability: Brazilian arabica moving into ICE warehouses still points to rebuilding certified stocks, and the proposed US tariffs on Brazil are the watch point for US-delivered flows.
events: US proposes surprise new tariffs on Brazilian imports (Reuters)
Brazilian arabica heading to ICE warehouses (Finimize, CNN Brasil)

cocoa.fundamental: Mar extended the rally to ~5,420 (+2%), with the slow pace of Ivory Coast port arrivals and dollar weakness driving short covering. Rising ICE certified stocks remain the offset; no new Ghana COCOBOD news, and no ICCO November quarterly bulletin found yet.
events: Cocoa settles higher on slower Ivory Coast deliveries (Barchart)
Dollar weakness sparks short covering in cocoa (Barchart)
